headline: LUNDIN GOLD Q2: 118,994 Oz At $4,359 Avg — $478M Revenue, $202M Adj. Earnings; AISC $1,176/oz; Guidance On Track (TSX: LUG)
snippet: Lundin Gold Inc. (TSX: LUG) reported Q2 2026 results on August 7, posting production of 118,994 ounces of gold at the Fruta del Norte underground mine in Ecuador and gold sales of 110,385 oz at an average realized price of $4,359 per ounce — $1,183/oz above AISC. Revenue totalled $478 million with adjusted earnings of $202 million. The mill processed 500,143 tonnes at an average head grade of 8.3 g/t gold with 89.1% recovery, achieving cash operating costs of $1,016/oz and AISC of $1,176/oz. The company is on track for full-year guidance and continues to advance the FDNS early-stage development, a mine-to-mill expansion study, and its largest-ever exploration programme. At a $4,300+ gold price, Fruta del Norte's high-grade single-asset profile is generating one of the strongest margins-per-ounce stories in the mid-tier gold sector.

headline: COPPER SMASHES ALL-TIME HIGH AT $6.90/LB — DRC Ban + El Teniente Halt; CNBC: 'This Is A Structural Supply Shock'
snippet: Copper futures broke to an all-time high near $6.90 per pound on August 6–7, 2026, driven by the convergence of three simultaneous supply shocks: the Democratic Republic of Congo's immediate ban on copper and cobalt concentrate exports (effective August 6), the ongoing suspension of Andes Norte development at Codelco's El Teniente mine in Chile with 3,000 workers idled and no restart date, and continued tariff-driven inventory hoarding in US warehouses. CNBC frames this record as structurally different from previous copper spikes: unlike the May 2026 tariff-driven pop, this move is simultaneously supply-side (mine output constrained across two of the world's largest producing regions) and demand-side (AI datacenter electrification, grid buildout). For junior copper developers, every week that global output faces multi-region simultaneous constraints pushes project NAVs priced on older copper assumptions further into undervalued territory.

headline: DRC BANS COPPER AND COBALT CONCENTRATE EXPORTS — Kamoa-Kakula Has Smelter Coverage; CMOC, Glencore Seek Waivers
snippet: The Democratic Republic of Congo — the world's second-largest copper producer and largest cobalt supplier — banned exports of copper and cobalt concentrates with immediate effect on August 6, 2026, under an order signed by three cabinet ministers as part of the government's push to force domestic refining and retain more mineral value onshore. The ban allows the Mines Minister to grant one-year waivers under 'strategic' circumstances. In practice, Congo exports most of its copper as finished cathodes (696,725 tonnes in Q1 2026) rather than concentrate (53,926 tonnes concentrate in Q1), but producers still shipping unprocessed material — including Glencore and CMOC — face immediate pressure to accelerate smelter construction or secure exemptions. Ivanhoe Mines separately clarified that Kamoa-Kakula's on-site smelter and the Lualaba Copper Smelter in Kolwezi now handle all of the operation's concentrate, removing the most prominent risk the initial Reuters headline implied for Ivanhoe shareholders.

headline: OSISKO GOLD HITS 95.93 g/t Au OVER 4.6m AT PROSERPINE — Open-Pit Target; 1km x 500m Footprint; 7km From Cariboo
snippet: Osisko Gold Group Inc. (TSX: OSK) confirmed on August 5, 2026 a new gold-mineralized system with open-pit potential at the Proserpine target in British Columbia, 7 km along strike to the southeast of the Cariboo Gold deposit. Standout hole PSP-26-004 cut 4.60 metres at 95.93 g/t gold from 110 metres depth, including 50 centimetres at 873 g/t; hole PSP-26-001 returned 8.60 metres at 5.46 g/t from 97 metres and 14.5 metres at 2.17 g/t from 572 metres. Results to date have defined a footprint approximately 1 kilometre along strike by 500 metres wide, open in all directions. Three rigs are advancing the 26,500-metre Proserpine programme to establish whether the target can add an open-pit component to complement the planned Cariboo underground development. Osisko shares surged on the announcement as the market repriced the broader Cariboo district's resource potential.

headline: EQUINOX POST-ORLA: 176,836 Oz Q2 — GUIDANCE RAISED To 870K-920K Oz; DIVIDEND UP 50%; 1.1M Oz Pro Forma Rate (TSX: EQX)
snippet: Equinox Gold Corp. (TSX: EQX) reported Q2 2026 results on August 5, delivering 176,836 ounces of gold — including 64,656 oz from Greenstone and 32,617 oz from Valentine — alongside its first post-Orla production guidance: 870,000 to 920,000 ounces for full-year 2026, reflecting five months of combined operations (August–December). On a pro forma basis assuming the Orla deal had closed January 1, the combined company would be tracking toward approximately 1.1 million ounces annually — firmly in senior gold producer territory. The quarterly dividend was raised by 50%. CEO Darren Hall will retire October 31 with Jason Simpson succeeding; Chuck Jeannes replaces Ross Beaty as Chairman. For retail investors, Equinox is a real-time case study in how transformative M&A looks when executed during a gold bull cycle: the Orla deal was structured at $4,000 gold and is now generating returns at $4,300+.

headline: LUNDIN MINING Q2: $1.2B REVENUE, $360M FREE CASH FLOW At Record $6.51/lb Copper — Adj. EBITDA $658M (TSX: LUN)
snippet: Lundin Mining Corp. (TSX: LUN) reported Q2 2026 results on August 5 with near-record quarterly metrics: revenue of $1.2 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $658 million, and free cash flow of $360 million, driven by a realized copper price of $6.51 per pound across production of 76,900 tonnes for the quarter. Year-to-date copper production stands at 157,000 tonnes; year-to-date adjusted EBITDA is $1.3 billion. At a $2.11/lb cash cost, Lundin is generating approximately $4.40/lb in gross margin — margins per pound that would have looked implausible when the 2026 budget was set. For retail investors holding junior copper developers on TSX-V, Lundin Mining's Q2 is a direct benchmark for what copper porphyry and VMS projects are worth in the ground at $6.50+ copper: the reserve value per tonne at these margins is materially different from the NAV models most juniors are still being valued against.

headline: CENTRAL BANKS ADDED 51 TONNES GOLD IN JUNE — 6th Straight Month; China's Actual Reserves May Top 5,000 Tonnes
snippet: Money Metals Exchange research, syndicated on GoldSeek and published August 5, 2026, shows World Gold Council data confirming central banks globally added a net 51 tonnes of gold in June — the sixth consecutive month of net purchasing. China's People's Bank officially raised reported holdings by 40 tonnes year-to-date to 2,346 tonnes (approximately 9% of total reserves). Money Metals analysts argue the undisclosed Chinese purchase programme places actual monetary gold holdings above 5,000 tonnes — more than double the official figure and approaching US official reserves of 8,133 tonnes. Goldman Sachs and BMO Capital Markets have both flagged China's undisclosed accumulation as a structural price support factor. For mining investors, six consecutive months of net central bank purchases at $4,000+ gold means the bid that broke the old price ceiling is now a recurring structural feature — not a crisis-driven spike.

headline: US'S LARGEST-EVER TUNGSTEN DEPOSIT — 3 Proton Lithium Holds 1.78M Tonnes; NASA Satellite Zone Blocks One-Third Of Claims
snippet: 3 Proton Lithium's Railroad Valley Minerals Project in Nevada holds an inferred tungsten resource of 1.78 million tonnes — more than five times the second-largest known US deposit — with an estimated in-situ value of approximately $152 billion at current tungsten prices, which have surged roughly 600% since February 2025 following China's tungsten export controls. The catch: a 17-square-mile section of the deposit lies beneath a 20-year mining ban imposed in 2023 at NASA's request for a satellite calibration zone, blocking access to approximately one-third of 3 Proton's mineral claims. The US administration has signalled priority interest in the project given China's approximately 80% control of global tungsten supply, but production is at least five years away pending resolution of the NASA land withdrawal. China dominates tungsten the way it dominates rare earth magnets: completely — making any Western tungsten discovery with even partial access to its resource a strategically meaningful critical minerals story at a moment when the Pentagon is actively seeking non-Chinese supply.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER TEST BULLISH BREAKOUTS On US-IRAN DEAL — FOREX.COM: $4,334 Key Resistance; Structure Has Shifted
snippet: FOREX.com's August 2026 technical analysis argues that gold and silver are testing a genuine structural breakout following the partial Strait of Hormuz reopening agreement: with oil prices easing and Treasury yields declining, two of gold's most consistent headwinds in 2026 have reversed simultaneously. Gold is breaking above the June-August consolidation range ($3,930–$4,200) and above the descending resistance line from March; $4,334 is the first meaningful resistance above current levels, and a sustained close above it would shift the tactical outlook from 'correcting bull' to 'resumed bull.' Silver is holding above both its 50-day and 100-day moving averages and the key $60 structural floor. For mining stock investors, the framing matters: gold miners typically see their most aggressive upside legs when gold breaks out of a multi-week consolidation into new ground — which is exactly what the current setup is attempting on NFP week.
